title: Week in review: Employment growth hits unexpected high after months of tepid gains
summary: We’re rounding up last week’s stories, including the impact of Grand Theft Auto VI’s release and religious accommodation for artificial intelligence tool use.

title: Workers are facing a ‘crisis of disengagement’
summary: Multiple factors are contributing to low engagement rates, including a low-hire job market, layoff anxiety, artificial intelligence uncertainty and burnout, per new research.

title: Dems must eye broad labor reform after midterm win, NLRB’s ex-top cop says
summary: Congress should consider passing a “PRO Act plus” while also minding state efforts to get involved in labor disputes, Jennifer Abruzzo said at an American Bar Association event.

title: Nearly two-thirds of HR leaders expect layoffs in 2027
summary: As companies plan payroll reductions, they’re also tightening their belts on severance packages while offering more extensive career transition services.

title: Workers will likely have to shoulder more of their healthcare costs, employers say
summary: As companies try to offset accelerating costs, employees face higher out-of-pocket expenses and the loss of some generous coverage options, a WTW survey found.

title: DOL final rule revamps antidiscrimination requirements for apprenticeships
summary: The U.S. Department of Labor issued a final rule to rescind “affirmative action requirements” for federally registered apprenticeships, effective Jan. 5.

title: ‘AI rebounding’ could cost companies
summary: Employers are replacing workers with artificial intelligence and then calling them back — but employees are demanding more money to return.

title: Change debt, not change fatigue, is driving burnout, research shows
summary: Unresolved issues from previous workplace upheaval may lead to increasingly heavy burdens for employees, a recent study found.

title: DOL announces applications open for apprentice payment program
summary: Relevant apprenticeship programs span the gamut from information technology to shipbuilding and defense to semiconductor production.

title: Lockheed Martin to pay nearly $30M to settle claims of discrimination against White workers
summary: The federal government alleged that HR personnel “exerted pressure on leaders” to remove nonminority employees initially selected for a compensation program and add minority workers.
